text:
Lenny was writing an autobiography--How to Talk Dirty and Influence People--which Playboy planned to serialize, then publish as a book, and they hired me as his editor. We met in Atlantic City, where he was taking Delaudid for lethargy, and he sent a telegram to a contact, with a phrase--DE LAWD IN DE SKY--as a code to send a doctor's prescription.

At a certain point he was acting paranoid and demanded that | take a lie-detector test, and | was paranoid enough to take him literally. | couldn't work with him if he didn't trust me. We got into an argument, and | left.

He sent a telegram that sounded like we were on the verge of divorce. "WHY CAN'T IT BE THE WAY IT USED TO BE?" he wrote. | agreed to try again, and in 1962 | flew to Chicago. Lenny was performing at the Gate of Horn, where he was asking the whole audience to take a lie-detector test.

Lenny was intrigued by the implications of an item in 7he Realist, an actual statement by Adolf Eichmann that he would have been "not only a scoundrel, but a despicable pig" if he hadn't carried out Hitler's orders.
Lenny wrote a piece for 7he Realist "Letter From a Soldier's Wife," namely Mrs. Eichmann pleading for compassion to spare her husband's

life.
